quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You will be able to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection against injury in a crash.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen by:

options.text: Letting the front tire lock up.
Using both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually to stop the shortest and safest distance. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: When riding, the best gear to wear is:

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Use a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good method.
Squeeze the tire to test it.
Compare the height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge before every ride. A tire that looks fine may actually be under-inflated, so you cannot rely on looking at it.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Using signals properly is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: When following a car, you should:

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride next to another car to be more visible.
Stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the center of their mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects the wearer from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles, along with protecting your face in a crash.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and show some leg.

questions.explanation: Wear pants that cover your entire legs and are made of leather or sturdy synthetic material. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but not so tight that it restricts movement.

questions.question: Why is space between your motorcycle and other vehicles important?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you rely on others to find hazards.
It requires you to go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: The back of the motorcycle will jerk side to side.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. This is very dangerous because it affects how well you can steer.

questions.question: If you drink four alcoholic drinks, how many drinks will be in your body after two hours?
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. So after two hours, at least two drinks will remain in your system.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: What is the best thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important action you can take to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing a motorcycle.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. It makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: What does wearing a helmet do?

options.text: It reduces your chances of head and neck injuries in a crash.
It increases your chances of neck injury in a crash.
It reduces your side vision by two-thirds.
It does not change your chances of head injury.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your chances of head and neck injuries in a crash.
questions.explanation: A proper, approved helmet reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. An approved helmet will not limit your vision for safe riding.

questions.question: Why should you keep space around your motorcycle?

options.text: It is only needed for beginning riders.
It gives you time and space to react to hazards.
It lets you weave through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time and space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle is your best protection. It gives you time and room to avoid any danger.
